blocks.orig: The Nyerere National Park, which used to be called Selous Game Reserve, is one of the largest protected areas in the world. It is located in southern Tanzania. Since 1982 it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This is due to its wildlife diversity and undisturbed nature you can find here. Although it lays far from Tanzania’s northern national parks, it is worth a visit. With a total area of 50,000 km2 and additional buffer zones, it’s even bigger than Denmark!
blocks.html: Formerly known as the Selous Game Reserve, Nyerere National Park ranks among the biggest protected areas on the planet. You will find it in the south of Tanzania. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982, thanks to the variety of wildlife and the untouched nature it holds. Even though it lies a long way from the national parks in the north of Tanzania, it is well worth the journey. Covering 50,000 km2, plus extra buffer zones, it is larger than Denmark!

blocks.orig: There are a huge number of wildlife animals you can find when on safari in Nyerere National Park. Lions, leopards, hippos, and crocodiles live in Nyerere. You can spot endangered black rhinos, hard-to-find East African wild dogs as well as hyenas. Cape buffaloes, Masai giraffes, wildebeests, and zebras live here too, the latter two are known by the great wildebeest migration! And of course it is home to impalas, large numbers of Lichtenstein’s hartebeests, waterbucks and sable antelope in addition to elands and bushbucks. It is much quieter here than in the other parks, so you definitely have the chance of a unique experience during your Tanzania vacation! Nyerere National Park was previously home to a very large number of many African bush elephants. Unfortunately, numbers have greatly reduced because of excessive poaching happening in the game reserve.
blocks.html: On safari in Nyerere National Park you can come across an enormous number of wild animals. The park is home to lions, leopards, hippos and crocodiles. You may see endangered black rhinos, elusive East African wild dogs and hyenas too. Cape buffaloes, Masai giraffes, wildebeests and zebras also live here; the last two are famous for the great wildebeest migration! Naturally there are impalas as well, together with large herds of Lichtenstein’s hartebeests, waterbucks and sable antelope, plus elands and bushbucks. Because Nyerere is much quieter than the other parks, a truly unique experience on your Tanzania holiday is well within reach! In the past the park sheltered a very large population of African bush elephants. Sadly, heavy poaching in the game reserve has caused their numbers to drop sharply.

blocks.orig: Nyerere National Park is home to thousands of birds. Scientists have recorded over 445 different birds species that live in the various habitats within Nyerere. The giant kingfishers, the pink backed pelican as well as the African skimmer live for instance near the lake areas. Along the sandbanks you will see the white-fronted bee-eater, fish eagle, carmine, ibises and palmnut vultures. The purple-crested turaco, yellow-billed stork, trumpeter hornbill, white-crowned spur-winged plovers, malachite kingfishers and various small waders are among the other water birds that you can see in Nyerere National Park, as well migrant species.
blocks.html: Thousands of birds live in Nyerere National Park. Researchers have counted more than 445 bird species across the park's different habitats. Near the lakes, for example, you will find the giant kingfisher, the pink-backed pelican and the African skimmer. On the sandbanks look out for the white-fronted bee-eater, fish eagle, carmine, ibises and palmnut vultures. Other water birds you may spot in Nyerere National Park include the purple-crested turaco, yellow-billed stork, trumpeter hornbill, white-crowned spur-winged plovers, malachite kingfishers and a range of small waders, alongside migratory species.

blocks.orig: Nyerere is also one of the few national parks where you can go on a boat safari. It is also one of the few parks that allows walking safari. It is an ideal trip if you want to enjoy the beautiful scenery of the Rufiji River with its many hippos, crocodiles and beautiful bird-life. The sunset can also be stunning from the boat – there is nothing quite like the serenity of the river while the sun dips below the horizon.
blocks.html: Nyerere is one of only a handful of national parks that offer boat safaris, and one of the few where walking safaris are permitted. If you would like to take in the lovely scenery of the Rufiji River, with its many hippos and crocodiles and its rich birdlife, this is the perfect outing. Sunset from the boat can be breathtaking as well – few things match the calm of the river as the sun sinks below the horizon.

blocks.orig: The best time to visit Nyerere is the dry season from June to October. The wildlife is easier to spot because the vegetation isn’t thick and the wild animals have gathered around the known water sources. Subsequent towards the end of the heavy rain, the roads are extremely impassable and many of the camps are closed as the wet season comes to an end. A good time to observe the scarce wild dogs is during their denning phase that begins in June and lasts till August.
blocks.html: The dry season, from June to October, is the best time for Nyerere. Animals are easier to see then, as the vegetation is thinner and wildlife gathers around the familiar water sources. Towards the end of the heavy rains the roads become almost impossible to use, and many camps shut as the wet season draws to a close. If you hope to see the rare wild dogs, their denning period from June to August is a good time to go.

blocks.orig: Travel Tips from our experts about Nyerere
blocks.html: Advice from our experts on Nyerere

blocks.orig: My name is Nixon, and I am a guide at Nyerere for 16 years. Most of our guests are impressed to see so many animals that live near the water, like the hippos and crocodiles. A walk to the Stiegler gorge is a welcome change from the jeep safari, and our clients do enjoy it.
blocks.html: I am Nixon, and I have been working as a guide in Nyerere for 16 years. Most of our guests are struck by how many animals live close to the water, such as the hippos and crocodiles. Our clients really enjoy a walk to the Stiegler Gorge, which makes a nice break from the jeep safari.

blocks.orig: How long to stay? At least 3 days, including your arrival and departure day, because those days are actually not full days. In this case, only the second day is a full day.
blocks.html: How many days should you stay? Plan at least 3 days, counting your arrival and departure days, since neither of those is a full day. That way only the second day is a complete one.

blocks.orig: Some tips on when and how you can best be /get there:
blocks.html: A few tips on the best time and way to get there:

blocks.orig: Avoid the wet months, I do advise going from June until October, because the park is not accessible during wet months. It becomes a swamp and even the animals do migrate to Mikumi or deep in the park.
blocks.html: Stay away during the wet months; my advice is to go between June and October, as the park cannot be reached in the rainy season. It turns into a swamp, and even the animals move away to Mikumi or into the depths of the park.

blocks.orig: Nyerere is far from all the other parks, they are all at least a full day driving away. I recommend flying, as this is in my opinion the only comfortable way.
blocks.html: Nyerere lies a long way from every other park; each of them is a full day's drive away at the very least. I would recommend flying, which I believe is the only comfortable option.

blocks.orig: Nyerere National Park in southern Tanzania is one of the largest game reserves in the world! It has numerous wildlife such as lions, leopards, the endangered black rhinos, hippos and crocodiles, East African wild dogs, Masai giraffes and many more!
blocks.html: In the south of Tanzania lies Nyerere National Park, one of the biggest game reserves on earth! Its wildlife is plentiful, with lions, leopards, endangered black rhinos, hippos and crocodiles, East African wild dogs, Masai giraffes and much more!

blocks.orig: The Rufiji River, which flows into the Indian Ocean opposite Mafia Island, crosses the entire reserve. Around this river is a swampy area with an enormous amount of crocodiles. The Stiegler Gorge is a special attraction here. This is a gap 100 meters deep and 100 meters wide.
blocks.html: The whole reserve is crossed by the Rufiji River, which reaches the Indian Ocean across from Mafia Island. The river is surrounded by swampland where huge numbers of crocodiles live. One of the highlights here is the Stiegler Gorge, a chasm 100 metres deep and 100 metres wide.
